title: Achan's Sin, Ai, and Covenant Renewal

date.label: Undated Joshua narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Achan’s act is narrated as cause of setback at Ai (Joshua 7:1–26)
Joshua 8:25 reports twelve thousand persons killed at Ai (Joshua 8:24–29)
MT Joshua places the Ebal altar ceremony after Ai battle (Joshua 8:30–35)

The Masoretic Text locates the Ebal altar in Joshua 8:30–35; 4Q47 preserves material in a different literary sequence near the Jordan crossing; Septuagint arrangement also requires careful witness-specific description. (Joshua 8:30–35)
claims.evidence: Mäkipelto, Tekoniemi and Tucker 2017, TC 22: 1–16, on large-scale transposition.

connections.note: The earlier instructions about devoted objects in Joshua 6 establish why Achan's taking of banned goods matters.
Deuteronomy 27 prescribes a covenant ceremony, while textual witnesses differ concerning Ebal and Gerizim and the placement of Joshua's ceremony.
Hosea's later reuse of the valley of Achor has a deliberate linguistic and theological relationship to Joshua 7, although it is not the same episode.
Joshua 9:1–2 is the immediate narrative continuation of the Ai episode, before the Gibeon story begins.
